key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the appellant only pointed out the location of the victim and did not carry a weapon or assault anyone, and that his presence at the site was explained by his house being adjacent to where the victim was hiding.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the witnesses as inconsistent, noting that PW-8 was not an eyewitness but believed what others said, and PW-7 was a hostile witness. The court found the reliance on PW-8's testimony unsustainable.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: Not stated; Trial judgment: 8.5.2015; High Court decision: 15.03.2019; Supreme Court decision: 6.9.2019
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Abir Phukan, Surya Prakash, Ashkrit Tiwari, Ms. Anisha Mathur for M/s Kmnp Law, Advs.; Counsel for the State: Debojit Borkakati, Vivek Sonkar, Advs.
investigation_status: Case No.145 of 1998 registered under Sections 147/148/149/324/326/302/201 of the IPC; decomposed body recovered and post-mortem conducted; charges framed against accused under Sections 147/148/324/302/201 read with Section 149 of the IPC
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted; High Court: Convicted some, gave benefit of doubt to others; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant was part of the unlawful assembly as he pointed out the location of the victim and assisted in the mob's search for him, thereby contributing to the victim's death.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the appellant was not part of the unlawful assembly, as he did not carry a weapon, did not assault anyone, and his presence at the scene was explained by his proximity to the victim's hiding place. The testimony of PW-8 was deemed unreliable as he did not witness the incident directly.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that mere presence at the scene or passive involvement does not suffice to establish participation in an unlawful assembly; there must be a common object and shared intention among the members of the assembly.
precedent_relied_upon: Subal Ghorai v. State of West Bengal (2013) 4 SCC 607; Ranjit Singh v. State of Punjab and Ors (2013) 16 SCC 752; C. Magesh and Ors. v. State of Karnataka (2010) 5 SCC 645
